content.text:
I checked both halves of RES-23 against the code at `227dfc8`, and both bugs are real. I haven't changed any code. Nothing was run: I read the source but didn't reproduce either bug.

## 1. The setup guess can name a host that doesn't exist

`fromRenderYaml` (`lib/base-url.js:92-102`) turns the first web service's `name` into `https://<name>.onrender.com`. The only check after that is `isPlausibleBaseUrl`, which looks at the URL's syntax and never makes a network request. The guess reaches the spec in two ways:

- **Interactive setup** (`steps/generate-oas.js:720-753`): the guess is pre-filled with "We found this in render.yaml - press enter to keep it". One Enter accepts a host nobody has checked, and it replaces the placeholder in the generated spec.
- **Agent setup** (`bin/restless.js:1276-1286`, `npx restless guide oas`): the agent is told to "verify it against the code". It can't: Render's `-tqme` suffix doesn't appear anywhere in the repo. After that, `register` (`bin/restless.js:1516`) only rejects local addresses, so it accepts the wrong host and also saves it as `baseUrl`.

Render is the weak source. The other sources come from names the developer chose or that are unique by design: a Vercel `alias`, ingress and Traefik hosts, and (I believe) Fly app names. Render service names are reused across accounts, so a taken name gets a random suffix. The current test (`tests/base-url.test.js:78`) only checks the string it builds, so nothing would catch this.

## 2. Changing the base URL in `update` never reaches the spec

- **Interactive:** `editSettings` changes `apiEntry.baseUrl` (`steps/update-interactive.js:356-359`), then calls `publish({ rootDir, apiEntry: chosenApi })` at line 386 without an `oasFile`.
- **Flags:** `--base-url` only updates the settings entry (`steps/update-flags.js:226-232`). `specFile` stays `null` unless `--oas` or `--refresh` is also given, so `syncProject` skips `pushOas` (`lib/project-sync.js:178`).
- `pushSettings` sends the settings to `/api/projects/:id/sync`. According to the issue, the app only uses that value as a label on the Settings page. That's in the app repo, so I couldn't check it from here.

So the CLI prints "✓ Settings synced", while `servers[0].url` stays the same locally and on the dashboard.

The workaround in the ticket is right: `--oas .restless/openapi.json` sets `specFile`, which makes `update` push the spec.

## Proposed fix (CLI side)

1. **Probe before using a guess.** Add a short HEAD/GET to the guessed host and treat any HTTP response as success (even a 404 shows the host exists). Do it in `guessBaseUrl` or where it's called. If the host doesn't resolve, show the guess without pre-filling it and say we couldn't reach it. In `guide oas`, say so in the instruction instead of offering it as a "deterministic guess". Doing it in `register` too would also catch a host the agent made up.
2. **Make a base URL change reach the spec.** When `baseUrl` changes and `isManagedSpec(apiEntry.oasFile)` is true, rewrite `servers[0].url` in that file and pass it as `oasFile` to `syncProject`. Do this in both `update-flags.js` and `update-interactive.js` (a shared helper would keep the two in sync). If the user maintains the spec themselves, don't edit it: print that `servers[0].url` still says X and how to change it.
3. Tests: one where the probe fails and the guess isn't pre-filled, and one where `update --base-url` on a managed spec rewrites `servers` and calls `pushOas`.

The ticket's longer-term question is still open: should the settings `baseUrl` or the spec's `servers` be the single source of truth? That belongs in the app repo. Step 2 keeps the two in sync until it's decided.

what a coding agent or a CI job needs. Run it inside Claude Code or Codex with

Part 2 is fixed: changing the base URL in `update` now updates the spec and pushes it. The full suite passes (1397 tests, including 14 new ones in `tests/spec-base-url.test.js`). Nothing is committed yet.

**What changed**

- **New `lib/spec-base-url.js`:** when the base URL changes, it writes the new URL into the spec's `servers[0].url`. It only does that for a spec the CLI wrote itself: a file in `.restless/` that the AI or a coding agent generated (or an old entry with no recorded source).
- **Other specs are left alone:** your own file, a fetched URL, a combined spec or framework output would get the old URL back on the next refresh. For those, `update` prints the URL the spec still has and says to fix it there and run `update --refresh`.
- **`lib/oas-source.js`:** each spec source type now says whether the CLI may edit its `servers`.
- **`update --base-url` (`steps/update-flags.js`):** runs after any `--oas`/`--refresh`, so it applies to the spec the project ends up with. A rewritten spec is pushed in the same run. The JSON output gains a `specServers` field saying what happened to the spec.
- **"Update Settings" (`steps/update-interactive.js`):** does the same on Submit if the Base URL field was opened or the chat editor changed the URL.
- The `--base-url` help line and the README now mention the spec.

**One behaviour to know about:** passing `--base-url` updates the spec even when settings already hold that URL. That's Larkspur's current state (settings right, spec stale), and without this the command would report "already matched" and change nothing. So `npx restless update --base-url https://larkspur-tqme.onrender.com` would now fix it, as well as the `--oas` workaround in the ticket.

The tests cover the helper and the `--base-url` path end to end with a mocked network. The interactive editor change has no automated test, and I haven't run it by hand.
